relation_statement: The optimizer's applied learning rate must equal the scheduler-defined value for the current step, including step 0 before the first scheduler.step().
observable_signal: optimizer.param_groups lr at the first optimizer step vs the scheduler's intended initial lr (warmup_min_lr)
validity_precondition: WarmupLR/LRRangeTest/OneCycle scheduler attached and optimizer constructed with a different (e.g. peak) lr
evidence_from_issue: schedulers do not initialize optimizer group lr at construction — first step uses original lr
evidence_from_fix: never wrote min_lr into param_groups; with 1e-4 peak lr and 0 warmup_min_lr the first update is ~10000x larger than intended

relation_statement: The block output must preserve the residual/identity path (output = sublayer(x) + x) and not overwrite the residual input under guard: attention norm applied.
observable_signal: Presence of the additive residual connection in block output vs input activation.
validity_precondition: transformer block with attention normalization
evidence_from_issue: Attention norm overwrites residual input — destroys identity path
evidence_from_fix: no root_cause provided; title indicates residual/identity path is destroyed

relation_statement: Attention outputs must remain finite (masked bias values must be representable in the compute dtype, e.g. finfo.min instead of -inf) under autocast mixed precision with padded/masked sequences.
observable_signal: NaN count in attention outputs / loss once masked tokens are present; presence of -inf bias entries in a bf16/fp16 SDP call witnesses the unsafe downcast.
validity_precondition: AMP/autocast (bf16 or fp16) with padded sequences requiring attention masking via scaled_dot_product_attention
evidence_from_issue: SDP attention bias not cast to autocast dtype, -inf downcasts to NaNs in mixed precision
evidence_from_fix: bias created in fp32 with -inf ... downcasting -inf propagates through softmax and produces NaNs; fix uses torch.finfo(target_dtype).min and casts the bias before the SDP call

relation_statement: The number of parameter elements stepped by the optimizer kernel must equal the parameter's total element count (numel), not just its first-dimension size.
observable_signal: fraction of parameter elements unchanged after an optimizer step despite nonzero gradients (all elements beyond the first row static)
validity_precondition: CPU Adam/Adagrad kernels applied to any parameter with ndim >= 2
evidence_from_issue: uses params.size(0) instead of numel() — only the first row of multi-dim params gets updated
evidence_from_fix: passed params_c.size(0) as the element count; for a (out, in) weight only `out` elements are stepped, the rest never receive an update

relation_statement: Label indices at boundary positions must lie in the offset (boundary-fused) vocabulary range in every forward branch under guard that boundary fusing is enabled.
observable_signal: label values at boundary-mask positions below the fused-vocabulary offset (offset never applied) in the first forward branch
validity_precondition: distillation decoder with fuse_boundaries enabled; applies to the label tensor before cross-entropy
evidence_from_issue: missed first-call label_offsets when fuse_boundaries enabled
evidence_from_fix: the offset-application path was duplicated but missed in the first forward branch, so cross-entropy compared against the wrong target indices for boundary tokens

relation_statement: The z-loss under reduction='mean' must equal the scalar masked mean of z_squared over non-ignored tokens whenever labels contain ignore_index tokens.
observable_signal: z-loss value (and shape: scalar vs vector) compared against a reference masked-mean recomputed from the same logits and labels
validity_precondition: compute_z_loss=True with reduction='mean' and labels containing ignore_index (-100) tokens
evidence_from_issue: cross_entropy_loss z-loss reduction='mean' uses wrong masked-mean formula
evidence_from_fix: buggy: z_squared / (labels != ignore).mean() returns vector divided by scalar, wrong scaling; fix: (z_squared * (labels != ignore)).mean() returns scalar masked-mean

relation_statement: An optimizer step and an outlier flag must be mutually exclusive: the optimizer must step exactly when the loss/grad-norm is NOT flagged as an outlier, whenever outlier skipping is enabled.
observable_signal: Optimizer step count vs batch count and the per-step is_outlier flag: parameters unchanged on normal batches (and updated only on outlier batches) witnesses the inverted gate.
validity_precondition: ce_loss_outlier_detector or grad_norm_outlier_detector enabled
evidence_from_issue: Outlier-loss skip-step logic inverted: optimizer steps only when loss IS an outlier
evidence_from_fix: should_step was AND-ed with is_outlier, meaning the optimizer only stepped on outlier steps and silently skipped normal training steps; fix negates is_outlier

relation_statement: The reduced gradient norm must count each gradient exactly once (reduction over the shard group, not WORLD) so the reported norm does not scale with the number of HSDP replicas.
observable_signal: Reported global grad norm vs the norm computed within a single replica's shard group; inflation by the replica count witnesses the wrong process group.
validity_precondition: FSDP HYBRID_SHARD/HYBRID_SHARD_ZERO2 with more than one model replica and gradient clipping or grad-norm metrics enabled
evidence_from_issue: clip_grads_and_collect_metrics reduces grad norm over the global PG instead of the HSDP shard PG
evidence_from_fix: each replica holds a full copy of the gradients, so reducing over WORLD double-counts grads across replicas; fix routes every reduce/all_reduce through an explicit process_group

relation_statement: Per-module low-precision scaling state (amax history / DelayedScaling recipe) must evolve identically whether the layer runs eagerly or via CUDA-graph replay, under FP4 training with graph capture enabled.
observable_signal: Per-module amax/scale values compared between graph replay and an eager reference step; monotone drift of FP4 scale away from target across replays witnesses the skipped recipe restoration.
validity_precondition: FP4 (NVFP4) DelayedScaling training with CUDA graphs enabled and FP8 inactive
evidence_from_issue: treats fp4_enabled as fp8 only, skipping the per-module FP-recipe restoration on FP4 paths so saved scaling factors drift each replay
evidence_from_fix: With FP4 active but FP8 inactive, the recipe restore branch was skipped, so each replay used a stale amax history ... every step shifted the FP4 scale away from the target

relation_statement: MoE expert outputs must be invariant to the TP degree, which requires gathering tokens across TP ranks even when sequence_parallel=False and EP=1.
observable_signal: expert input token count on each TP rank vs the full gathered token count (each rank processes only its local slice)
validity_precondition: MoE with GroupedGEMM experts and sequence_parallel=False
evidence_from_issue: MoE GroupedGEMM produces wrong outputs without sequence_parallel even when TP>1
evidence_from_fix: with TP>1 but SP=False (and EP=1) neither predicate was True, so expert tokens were never gathered across TP ranks and each TP rank produced wrong (incomplete) MoE outputs

relation_statement: Parameter storage dtype must match the configured mixed-precision dtype (bf16 config must materialize bf16 params) under the DSL config path, just as the legacy CLI path guarantees.
observable_signal: Dtype of materialized model parameters at init compared to mixed_precision_dtype (fp32 params under bf16 config witness the violation), plus roughly doubled parameter memory footprint.
validity_precondition: Hybrid model built via the Python DSL recipe API with mixed_precision_dtype='bf16' and params_dtype left at default
evidence_from_issue: does not derive params_dtype from mixed_precision_dtype, so models with mixed_precision_dtype='bf16' silently keep params_dtype=fp32
evidence_from_fix: produced a TransformerConfig with bf16=True but params_dtype=torch.float32 ... parameters materialized in fp32 and cast on every forward, doubling memory and changing numerics relative to the legacy path

relation_statement: The gradient submitted for reduction must be the accumulated fp32 gradient buffer, not the raw bf16 param.grad, whenever grad_accum_dtype=fp32 with CPU offload.
observable_signal: reduced gradient compared against the fp32 accumulated buffer contents (precision loss and stale values witness violation)
validity_precondition: bf16 model with grad_accum_dtype=fp32, ZeRO stage 1 with CPU offload, and a parameter larger than reduce_bucket_size
evidence_from_issue: bf16+ZeRO1+CPU offload silently routes through bf16 wrapper; extra-large param uses raw param.grad instead of reduction grad
evidence_from_fix: reduction code took extra_large_param_to_reduce.grad directly instead of routing through get_gradient_for_reduction(); the accumulated fp32 grad was bypassed and the raw bf16 grad was reduced

relation_statement: The gradient scaling factor must equal 1/(dp_size*cp_size), matching the span of the gradient reduction collective, when context parallelism is enabled.
observable_signal: effective gradient magnitude over-scaled by cp_size relative to a CP=1 reference
validity_precondition: sample-mean loss (calculate_per_token_loss=False) with DistributedOptimizer or average_in_collective enabled
evidence_from_issue: target_gradient_scaling_factor uses get_data_parallel_world_size without context_parallel, so gradients are over-scaled by cp_size
evidence_from_fix: the gradient reduction collective spans the dp*cp ranks, so gradients should be divided by dp_size*cp_size; only dividing by dp_size leaves a residual factor of cp_size in the parameter updates

relation_statement: The accumulated weight gradient must equal the sum of per-microbatch gradients written into the live main_grad buffer under FSDP gradient accumulation fusion.
observable_signal: main_grad buffer staleness (data_ptr differs from the per-iteration reconstructed buffer) and accumulated wgrad vs reference sum of microbatch gradients
validity_precondition: Megatron-FSDP parameters (FSDP DTensor) with gradient_accumulation_fusion in linear backward
evidence_from_issue: FSDP grad accumulation fusion missing main_grad creation in linear backward
evidence_from_fix: main_grad must be reconstructed in-place via weight.get_main_grad() each iteration; without this, main_grad pointed to a stale buffer, so accumulated weight gradients were wrong

relation_statement: The offloaded gradient partition must accumulate rather than overwrite contributions from every backward call within a step when manual gradient accumulation is used under ZeRO-1/2 CPU offload.
observable_signal: gradient norm at optimizer step vs the sum of per-microstep gradient contributions (norm underestimated on violation)
validity_precondition: ZeRO-1/2 with CPU offload and manual gradient accumulation (multiple backward calls, micro_step_id > 0)
evidence_from_issue: ZeRO-1/2 CPU-offload gradient norm underestimated with manual GA
evidence_from_fix: copy_grads_in_partition only accumulates when ga_steps > 1, misses micro_step_id > 0 case

relation_statement: The data-loader position counters must be reset to zero at the start of each evaluation pass under guard that the evaluator reuses a loader whose previous pass was truncated.
observable_signal: tokens_processed/batches_processed value at eval-pass start being nonzero; differing eval scores for repeated evals of the same checkpoint
validity_precondition: evaluator runs multiple passes over the same loader with eval_duration truncating each pass
evidence_from_issue: second eval pass starts mid-stream, evaluating a different subset
evidence_from_fix: Evaluator.__iter__ called reshuffle() but did not reset(); counters from the previous truncated eval persisted so the next pass started at a stale offset

relation_statement: soft_target_probs must preserve floating-point dtype through as_tensor and not be truncated to int under guard: non-bool numpy float array.
observable_signal: Dtype of the resulting target tensor and whether probabilities were floored to integers.
validity_precondition: soft target probabilities passed through local as_tensor()
evidence_from_issue: soft_target_probs silently truncated from float to int by as_tensor()
evidence_from_fix: local as_tensor casts non-bool numpy arrays via astype(np.int_), destroying float probabilities

relation_statement: The input gradient produced by a frozen-weight TP linear must be all-reduced so all TP ranks pass the identical summed dgrad to upstream layers.
observable_signal: cross-TP-rank difference of grad_input leaving the frozen-weight linear backward
validity_precondition: column/row-parallel linear with frozen weights (requires_grad=False) on the asynchronous all-reduce path
evidence_from_issue: LinearWithFrozenWeight backward skips TP all-reduce of dgrad when TP>1
evidence_from_fix: backward computed grad_input without the cross-TP all-reduce; downstream layers received TP-rank-local input gradients instead of the summed gradient

relation_statement: Each context-parallel rank's rotary embedding slice must cover exactly the token positions of its own sequence partition, so forward activations are invariant to the CP degree.
observable_signal: Per-CP-rank rotary position index range compared against the rank's sequence-partition offsets (or activations vs a CP=1 reference); slicing the wrong axis / wrong cp_group witnesses the mismatch.
validity_precondition: Multimodal rotary embedding (mrope) with context_parallel_world_size > 1 and sequence dimension at index 0 post-transpose
evidence_from_issue: slices rotary embedding along the wrong dimension and omits cp_group when CP is enabled, so each CP rank sees the wrong rotary position embedding
evidence_from_fix: get_pos_emb_on_this_cp_rank was called with seq_dim=1 and no cp_group ... each CP rank ended up with a rotary slice that does not correspond to its own sequence partition

relation_statement: The auxiliary z-loss must be normalized by batch_size_in_tokens rather than num_micro_batches whenever softmax_auxiliary_loss is enabled.
observable_signal: ratio of z-loss to main loss, which inflates by batch_size_in_tokens/num_micro_batches under the buggy normalizer
validity_precondition: softmax_auxiliary_loss=True and num_micro_batches != batch_size_in_tokens
evidence_from_issue: Trainer.train_micro_batch divides z_loss by num_micro_batches instead of batch_size_in_tokens
evidence_from_fix: z_loss / num_micro_batches scales auxiliary loss by gradient accumulation count, not by token count; with T >> num_micro_batches, z_loss dominates loss and corrupts training

relation_statement: Each loss component must be divided by the position count of its own granularity (byte positions for byte loss, patch positions for patch loss) under guard that multi-granularity losses are combined.
observable_signal: ratio of byte-loss to patch-loss magnitudes deviating from the configured weighting by the byte/patch position-count mismatch factor
validity_precondition: distillation transformer with a patch-level loss divisor configured alongside byte-level losses
evidence_from_issue: patch loss div factor used input_ids.numel() — wrong scaling for byte-level losses
evidence_from_fix: the correct denominator is the number of byte positions, with an analogous division by patch positions for the patch loss; the mismatch silently mis-weighted byte vs patch loss components

relation_statement: Each microbatch's expert weight gradient must be accumulated exactly once; the wgrad accumulate-and-reduce hooks must fire on the modules owning the parameters so param.grad is cleared.
observable_signal: residual param.grad after the hooks should have cleared it; expert wgrad norm doubled relative to a single-count reference on subsequent iterations
validity_precondition: grouped-linear fused-ops path with DDP overlap_grad_reduce (wgrad hooks) and multiple microbatches in MoE training
evidence_from_issue: fused-ops backward_dw skips wgrad hooks on the original linear modules, so DDP never zeros param.grad and AccumulateGrad double-counts
evidence_from_fix: hooks were registered on the original fc1/fc2 modules but backward_dw ran on new instances; hooks never fired, param.grad was not cleared, and AccumulateGrad added again into main_grad, silently double-counting expert weight gradients

relation_statement: The fp32 residual stream must preserve its dtype through bias-dropout-add rather than being downcast to the bf16 branch dtype.
observable_signal: output dtype of the bias-dropout-add result (bf16 instead of fp32) when the residual is fp32
validity_precondition: fp32 residual connection combined with a bf16 compute branch in bias-dropout-add
evidence_from_issue: fp32 residual connection silently downcast to bf16
evidence_from_fix: _bias_dropout_add_func downcasts residual to x.dtype (bf16) instead of upcasting x to residual.dtype (fp32)

relation_statement: Every trainable parameter of a module must receive its designated initialization before training starts under guard that subclass modules are dispatched by the init method.
observable_signal: weight statistics of the extra projection matrices at step 0 showing uninitialized (empty-allocation) values instead of the designated init distribution
validity_precondition: attention subclass with additional projections handled by an isinstance-ordered init dispatch
evidence_from_issue: MultiHeadLatentAttention init dispatched to Attention branch — wrong layers initialized
evidence_from_fix: the subclass branch was never reached because isinstance matched the parent class first; wq_a, wkv_a, wkv_b were never initialized, left at dtype-empty allocation values

relation_statement: Each parameter's gradient must be routed into the reduction bucket belonging to that parameter's own group under multi-group sharded training.
observable_signal: group index bound in each backward hook vs the parameter's actual group id; per-group reduced-gradient mismatch when groups > 1
validity_precondition: sharded-gradient training (ZeRO stage 3) with more than one parameter group
evidence_from_issue: backward hook closure captures stale group index `i` — gradient routed to wrong reduction bucket
evidence_from_fix: `i` was Python-late-bound inside the closure, every hook fired with the same final value of `i`, routing earlier groups' gradients into the last group's bucket
